key_insight: No reconstruction method wins across all flow regimes: classical estimators remain competitive, while learned models gain an advantage as sensors become sparser or less informative.
engineering_relevance: Sparse-sensor flow reconstruction should be selected by flow regime, observed variables, uncertainty needs and computational budget—not accuracy alone.
method: Benchmark 10 learned and 5 classical methods across cylinder wake, 2D Kolmogorov turbulence and 3D isotropic turbulence.
Use shared leakage-controlled splits and sensor draws for fair comparisons.
Evaluate per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and computational cost.
evidence_signal: Classical methods lead on the cylinder wake, inverse-distance weighting matches top learned methods on observed 3D channels, and Kolmogorov rankings differ between pointwise error and probabilistic scoring.
watch_item: Generative ensembles can remain underdispersed, larger sampling budgets increase cost, and full-grid reconstruction can exceed memory limits at scale.
paper_title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
